title: Nepal’s UN Ambassador meets Secretary-General António Guterres, discusses climate action and multilateral cooperation - The Annapurna Express
description: Nepal’s UN Ambassador meets Secretary-General António Guterres, discusses climate action and multilateral cooperation  The Annapurna Express
publisher.title: The Annapurna Express
full_article:
New York, October 29 — Nepal’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Lok Bahadur Thapa, met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Thursday and discussed multilateral cooperation, climate action and Nepal’s response to recent disasters.

According to a statement issued by the Permanent Mission of Nepal to the United Nations in New York, Ambassador Thapa commended Guterres for his principled leadership, steadfast commitment to multilateralism, spirit of solidarity and resolve to ensure that no one is left behind.

During the meeting, Thapa expressed the Government of Nepal’s profound appreciation for the assistance extended by the United Nations system in the aftermath of the country’s recent disasters. He also reaffirmed Nepal’s commitment to multilateralism, the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and collective international efforts to address shared global challenges.

Guterres expressed heartfelt condolences over the recent disasters in Nepal and commended the country’s active and constructive role in advancing multilateral cooperation, according to the statement.

The UN chief acknowledged Nepal’s contributions to the multilateral system, including its presidency of the UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), chairmanship of the Least Developed Countries (LDCs), facilitation of the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4), and chairmanship of the UN General Assembly’s First Committee.

He also recognized Nepal’s sustained advocacy for climate action and its longstanding contributions to international peace and security as one of the leading troop- and police-contributing countries to UN peacekeeping operations.

Recalling his visit to the base camp of Mount Everest three years ago, when he drew global attention to the devastating impacts of climate change in the Himalayas, Guterres underscored the urgent need for concerted and ambitious global climate action.

Both Thapa and Guterres emphasized the importance of strengthening early warning systems, enhancing resilience to climate-induced disasters, and fostering greater international solidarity, consensus and ambition to advance the global climate agenda.

The meeting reaffirmed the importance of international cooperation in addressing climate change, disaster risks and other shared global challenges, the statement said.

title: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News - Khabarhub
description: Economic Digest: A Snapshot of Nepal’s Business News  Khabarhub
publisher.title: Khabarhub
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Economic Digest presents a brief yet comprehensive roundup of major business developments in Nepal, delivered in clear and accessible summaries.

Nepal’s economic outlook presents a mixed picture, combining positive financial market performance and infrastructure investment with mounting external trade pressures and climate-related challenges. The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) rose by 33.29 points to 2,664.06, supported by broad-based gains, while gold and silver prices also increased, reflecting changing domestic market conditions.

However, the external sector remains under pressure. The trade deficit widened by 34.71 percent to Rs 532.49 billion in the first three months of the fiscal year, as imports grew substantially despite faster export growth. Heavy dependence on China and India for electric vehicles and smartphones further highlights Nepal’s limited diversification of import sources. Although Birgunj Customs exceeded its monthly revenue target, its cumulative collection remained below target, underscoring the importance of sustained trade activity for public finances.

Climate vulnerability presents another major concern. Recent disasters reportedly caused USD 2.7 billion in losses, while reconstruction needs reached USD 4.8 billion. Proposed damage assessments and international climate financing could support recovery, but effective implementation remains crucial.

Meanwhile, underground power infrastructure, industrial capacity utilization and tourism promotion indicate opportunities for longer-term growth. Nevertheless, budgetary priorities, including the disparity between medicine procurement and tourism-related religious infrastructure, raise questions about resource allocation. Overall, Nepal needs stronger export competitiveness, diversified trade, resilient infrastructure and balanced public spending to achieve sustainable economic growth.

NEPSE gains 33 points as turnover reaches Rs 7.47 billion

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index rose by 33.29 points, or 1.26 percent, to close at 2,664.06 on Wednesday, with total turnover reaching Rs 7.468 billion. Share prices of 241 companies advanced, while 35 declined and three remained unchanged. Of the 13 sectoral indices, only the trading subindex ended in negative territory, while the remaining sectors recorded gains. A total of 19.40 million shares were traded through 63,744 transactions during the session. Beni Hydropower posted the highest gain, rising by 15 percent, while Prime Debenture recorded the steepest decline at 2.96 percent. Liberty Energy led turnover, with shares worth Rs 325 million traded at Rs 250 per share.

Gold rises to Rs 283,200 per tola, silver reaches Rs 3,980

Gold and silver prices increased in Nepal’s domestic market on Wednesday, according to the Federation of Nepal Gold and Silver Dealers’ Association. The price of gold rose by Rs 900 per tola, from Rs 282,300 on Tuesday to Rs 283,200 on Wednesday. One tola is equivalent to approximately 11.66 grams. Silver prices also edged up, gaining Rs 10 per tola to reach Rs 3,980 from Rs 3,970 a day earlier. The latest rates reflect an increase in the prices of both precious metals in the domestic market.

Foreign trade deficit rises to Rs 532.49 billion amid import surge

Nepal’s foreign trade deficit increased by 34.71 percent during the first three months of the current fiscal year, reaching Rs 532.494 billion, compared with the figure reported for the same period last year, according to the Department of Customs. Merchandise imports climbed by 38.18 percent to Rs 646.7 billion from Rs 468 billion in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, exports grew by 57.03 percent to Rs 114.2 billion, up from Rs 72.78 billion. The country’s total foreign trade turnover increased by 40.71 percent to Rs 761 billion during the review period, reflecting substantial growth in both imports and exports.

Nepal reports USD 2.7 billion in disaster losses, calls for greater space-data sharing

Nepal has urged regional cooperation in using satellite observations and ground-based measurements to monitor climate-related hazards in the Himalayas, while highlighting the severe human and economic toll of recent disasters. Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha made the remarks while addressing the Fifth Ministerial Conference on Space Applications for Sustainable Development in Asia and the Pacific in Bangkok, Thailand, on Wednesday. Shrestha said recent disasters had claimed more than 1,400 lives and left over 5,000 people missing. According to the Rapid Damage and Need Assessment, the total impact of the disasters amounted to USD 2.7 billion, while USD 4.8 billion would be required for recovery and reconstruction. He stressed the importance of combining satellite data with ground measurements to monitor glacier-related hazards and improve disaster preparedness. He cited the August 26 debris flow from Langtang Lirung into the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers, as well as the October 11 landslide in the Budhi Gandaki area. Nepal is scheduled to co-host a regional dialogue on Thursday, October 29, to further discuss these issues.

Gas dealers welcome VAT billing directive, urge consumers to collect receipts

The Gas Dealers Federation of Nepal has welcomed Nepal Oil Corporation’s (NOC) directive requiring sellers to issue value-added tax (VAT) bills for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sales, describing the move as an important step toward improving transparency and accountability in the sector. In a press statement issued on Wednesday, the federation said the directive would help make LPG transactions more systematic and transparent. The NOC’s LP Gas and Aviation Department issued the instruction to gas industries on October 25, requiring them to ensure that sellers provide bills to customers. The directive followed a growing number of complaints about sellers failing to issue bills or invoices after selling LPG. Federation President Gyaneshwar Aryal urged gas entrepreneurs to comply fully with the requirement. He also encouraged consumers to request and collect bills whenever purchasing LPG, saying regular billing would promote accountability and strengthen business practices.

Parliamentary panel seeks detailed flood damage assessment as Nepal eyes USD 20 million fund

A special committee of the National Assembly has directed the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment to submit detailed, ward-level assessments of flood damage across 49 affected wards. At a meeting on Wednesday, committee Chair Krishna Prasad Poudel said field inspections would be conducted after the ministry submits comprehensive reports on losses to agriculture, livestock, aquatic life, farmland and biodiversity. Ministry Secretary Rajendra Prasad Mishra said assessments were underway, with damage being calculated using cultivation records and prevailing market prices. Ministry spokesperson Maheshwar Dhakal said Nepal had an opportunity to submit a proposal worth USD 20 million to the international Loss and Damage Fund. He also emphasized the need to advance climate justice and strengthen regional cooperation. The committee plans to conduct field visits to Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, following consultations with the ministry. The dates for the proposed visits should be confirmed, as the October 3–7 schedule provided in the original report appears inconsistent with the stated timeline.

Electric vehicle imports reach Rs 16.07 billion in three months

Nepal imported electric vehicles worth Rs 16.069 billion during the first three months of the current fiscal year, despite disruptions to northern trade routes caused by monsoon-related flood damage in Rasuwa and Mustang districts. According to customs records, the government collected Rs 9.414 billion in revenue from electric vehicle imports during the review period. China remained the largest source of imported electric vehicles, supplying 9,552 units worth Rs 11.657 billion. India ranked second, exporting 3,162 units valued at Rs 3.282 billion. Additional electric vehicles were imported from Thailand, the United States and other countries.

Smartphone imports worth Rs 18.81 billion, with China leading supply

Nepal imported 811,267 smartphones worth more than Rs 18.81 billion during the three-month review period, according to official customs data. China was the largest supplier, accounting for 701,244 units valued at over Rs 14.56 billion. India followed with 105,829 smartphones worth more than Rs 3.84 billion. Combined, the two neighbouring countries supplied 807,073 smartphones, representing the overwhelming majority of Nepal’s total imports in the category. Other suppliers included the United States, with 933 units; Japan, with 922; Australia, with 629; Malaysia, with 556; the United Arab Emirates, with 321; South Korea, with 181; Great Britain, with 162; Canada, with 105; and Qatar, with 74. The figures underscore Nepal’s heavy reliance on China and India for smartphone supplies.

Birgunj Customs exceeds monthly revenue target

The Birgunj Customs Office collected Rs 26.73 billion in revenue between September 17 and October 17, exceeding its monthly target of Rs 26.46 billion by 1.02 percent, according to the office’s chief customs administrator. Fuel imports were the largest revenue contributor, generating Rs 2.29 billion. Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) imports followed with Rs 1.8 billion, while bitumen imports generated Rs 1.4 billion. Imports of apples and pears contributed Rs 500 million. Despite surpassing its monthly target, the office fell short of its cumulative revenue goal for the first three months of the fiscal year. By the end of the review period, it had collected Rs 69.13 billion against a target of Rs 70.56 billion. The office attributed its monthly performance partly to increased economic activity during the festive season.

Pokhara underground power lines extend to 165.7 kilometres

The Nepal Electricity Authority has installed 165.7 kilometres of underground power lines in Pokhara under a project aimed at modernizing and strengthening the city’s electricity distribution system. Electricity is currently being supplied through 55.2 kilometres of the underground network. The work is being carried out under the Pokhara-Bharatpur Distribution System Reinforcement Project, which aims to install underground power lines across 223 kilometres in Pokhara. According to the project’s chief engineer, physical progress in the city has reached 82 percent, with completion targeted for mid-May. Around 6,000 households are expected to receive electricity through the underground network. More than 400 households along sections of the Prithvi Highway and several major roads are already receiving power through the system. The project also includes the installation of optical fibre infrastructure for telephone, cable television and internet services, alongside the removal of overhead wires and old utility poles. Funded through concessional loans from the Asian Development Bank, the Pokhara component has a budget of Rs 1.70 billion. However, extending underground power lines throughout the Pokhara Valley would require an estimated investment of more than Rs 5 billion, according to Subedi.

Sudurpashchim allocates Rs 50.1 million for medicines and Rs 1.15 billion for tourism

The Sudurpashchim Provincial Government has allocated Rs 50.1 million for procuring essential medicines for health facilities and hospitals in its fiscal year 2026/27 budget, while setting aside Rs 1.15 billion for tourism infrastructure development. The tourism allocation is intended to support the development of more than 600 local temples and religious shrines across the province. Of the funding for medicines, Rs 29.2 million will be managed by the Provincial Health Logistics Management Centre. An additional Rs 1 million has been allocated to district health offices in Bajura, Bajhang, Baitadi, Doti, Dadeldhura and Achham for the distribution of free medicines. The budget priorities have drawn criticism in provincial political circles and on social media, particularly over the disparity between spending on religious infrastructure and essential healthcare. The tourism allocation is nearly 23 times the amount earmarked for medicines, despite continuing shortages of routine treatments for chronic conditions such as hypertension and diabetes in rural health facilities.

Nuwakot officials receive training on flood relief grants

An orientation programme on the implementation of the Bhote Koshi Flood Victims Housing and Livelihood Grant Distribution Process, 2026, and the effective use of the Resource Management Information System (RMIS) was held in Nuwakot on Wednesday. The programme was chaired by Nuwakot Chief District Officer Shambhu Prasad Regmi and attended by officials from local governments and wards affected by the floods. Participants were briefed on procedures for distributing housing and livelihood grants to flood victims, as well as the effective use of RMIS to manage relevant information and resources. The initiative aims to support the transparent and efficient implementation of assistance programmes for affected households. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority organized the programme in coordination with the District Administration Office, Nuwakot. CRS Nepal and the Nuwakot District Chapter of the Nepal Red Cross Society provided technical support.

Tourism Board invites companies to participate in China International Travel Mart

The Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) has invited tourism companies to apply for participation in the China International Travel Mart (CITM), scheduled to take place from December 12 to 14, 2026. The participation fee has been set at Rs 125,000 per company. The board will select up to seven companies through a lucky draw scheduled for November 4 at 10 a.m. at its office. Online applications will open at 10 a.m. on October 29, with the deadline set for November 3. Interested companies must submit their applications and supporting documents through the NTB’s online portal. Required documents include company registration certificates, VAT/PAN registration, tax clearance for fiscal year 2024/25, a valid operating licence and a foreign currency exchange certificate issued by Nepal Rastra Bank. Selected companies must complete their payments online within the deadline specified by the board. Participating companies will be responsible for their own travel, accommodation and visa expenses.

Industrial capacity utilization in Koshi rises to 43.1 percent

The average capacity utilization of industrial enterprises in Koshi Province increased to 43.1 percent in fiscal year 2025/26, up from 41.8 percent in the previous fiscal year, according to a study published by Nepal Rastra Bank. Soybean oil manufacturing recorded the highest capacity utilization rate at 118 percent, while vegetable ghee production posted the lowest at 6.5 percent. Industrial output also increased across several sectors. Production of soybean oil rose by 45.3 percent, mustard oil by 11.9 percent, processed rice by 28.1 percent, animal feed by 15 percent, sugar by 13.6 percent, noodles by 12.6 percent, and plastic goods by 14.5 percent. Output of domestic metal products recorded a particularly sharp increase of 287.8 percent. Outstanding industrial credit extended by banks and financial institutions reached Rs 173 billion by the end of the previous fiscal year, accounting for 27.2 percent of total lending. Koshi Province’s gross domestic product growth was provisionally estimated at 3.13 percent. The province had 1,836 bank branches, with total deposits reported at Rs 6.419 billion and total lending at Rs 6.393 billion.

Teacher Service Commission speeds up review of promotion appeals filed by 6,000 teachers

The Teacher Service Commission has expedited the publication of revised promotion results following appeals filed by nearly 6,000 teachers whose rankings were determined through performance evaluations. Commission spokesperson Parshuram Tiwari said the commission was publishing revised rankings for promotions based on the 75 percent performance evaluation criterion after decisions were made by the secretariats of promotion recommendation committees. Under Chapter 15 of the Teacher Service Commission Operating Procedures, 2022, as amended, the commission is examining submitted documents and supporting evidence before finalizing promotion results for teachers at the relevant levels and in their respective districts. The review process had remained stalled for six months because the commission lacked officeholders. The government appointed Hari Prasad Lamsal as chairperson, along with other officials, on September 10, filling the vacant positions and allowing the process to move forward.

Nepal and France discuss cooperation in aviation and scientific research

Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal and newly appointed French Ambassador to Nepal Françoise Puig-Inza discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in aviation, climate action, scientific research and multilateral affairs during a meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Wednesday. According to the ministry, Khanal congratulated Puig-Inza on her appointment and wished her a successful tenure in Nepal. The meeting also covered areas of mutual interest, with both sides exploring opportunities to expand cooperation and deepen relations between Nepal and France.

NATHM delegation explores tourism cooperation with Bahrain

A delegation from the Nepal Academy of Tourism and Hotel Management (NATHM) visited Bahrain from October 25 to 27 to explore academic and professional cooperation with Vatel Bahrain Tourism and Business School and strengthen bilateral engagement in tourism-related sectors. The delegation was led by NATHM Executive Director and Principal Dibya Raj Pokhrel. Other members included Bipin Nepal, director of the Mountaineering Studies Division, and Damber Raj Bhatta, research and incubation officer. On October 26, the delegation met Mohamed Rashed Alsowaidi, chief of Asian and Pacific Affairs at Bahrain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Sara Ahmed Buhiji, CEO of the Bahrain Tourism and Exhibitions Authority. Nepali Ambassador to Bahrain Tirtha Raj Wagle and embassy Second Secretary Keshav Raj Panthi also participated in the meetings. Discussions focused on potential cooperation in education, adventure tourism, hospitality, mountaineering, yoga and wellness. The delegation also visited the Embassy of Nepal in Manama for an interactive briefing as part of its efforts to strengthen institutional and professional ties between the two countries.

Autumn climbing permits generate Rs 318 million in royalties from 44 Himalayan peaks

Nepal collected Rs 318 million in government royalties from mountaineering permits issued to 1,410 climbers from 76 countries during the autumn climbing season. The climbers were part of 161 expedition teams preparing to scale 44 Himalayan peaks. According to a branch officer at the Department of Tourism, the permits were issued to 1,069 male and 341 female climbers, generating more than USD 2 million in revenue. Manaslu, standing at 8,163 metres, attracted the largest number of climbers, with 500 mountaineers in 43 expedition teams. Permits for the peak generated Rs 225.8 million in royalties. Other major royalty contributions included Rs 8.4 million from Dhaulagiri I, Rs 688,050 from Makalu, Rs 7.4 million from Himlung Himal and Rs 57.6 million from Ama Dablam. Permits were also issued for expeditions to Puma Hiunchuli, Baruntse and Thorang Peak. Among the permitted climbers, 141 were from China, 130 from France, 119 from the United States, 108 from Russia and 96 from Great Britain. Italy and Switzerland each accounted for 47 climbers, followed by Poland with 41, India with 40, Japan with 35 and Nepal with 33.

Keroun substation completed in Morang to strengthen power supply in eastern Nepal

Construction of the 132 kV Keroun substation in Kanepokhari Rural Municipality-2, Morang, has been completed to improve electricity reliability, voltage stability and power distribution in the district and surrounding areas of eastern Nepal. The substation is scheduled to be charged on October 31 and November 1. The process requires looping-in and looping-out operations on the Duhabi-Damak 132 kV transmission line. Temporary power interruptions are expected from 4 a.m. to noon during the system integration work, affecting Jhapa, Ilam, Panchthar, Taplejung and parts of Morang, including Urlabari and Pathari. The facility houses two 132/33 kV transformers, each with a capacity of 63 MVA, and one 33/11 kV transformer with a capacity of 22.5 MVA, providing a combined installed capacity of 148.5 MVA. The project was completed at an estimated cost of Rs 1 billion through joint investment by the Government of Nepal and the Nepal Electricity Authority, supplemented by concessional loans from the Asian Development Bank.

Industrial area authority restricts non-manufacturing activities on leased land

Industrial Area Management Limited has introduced stricter rules to prevent non-manufacturing businesses from operating on land allocated to industrial enterprises in state-established industrial zones. Under the revised provisions, businesses such as vehicle service centres, workshops and commercial showrooms operating on industrial plots will be required to convert their operations into approved manufacturing industries within a five-year grace period. Enterprises that fail to meet the requirement will face cancellation of their lease agreements, according to the authority’s general manager. The policy aims to ensure that limited industrial land is used primarily for productive manufacturing, supply-chain development, value addition and import substitution. The reform also seeks to address concerns over the use of publicly supported industrial infrastructure for commercial activities unrelated to manufacturing.

Lumbini Cable Car sees 24 percent rise in Indian visitors

The number of Indian visitors using the Lumbini Cable Car increased by 24 percent in fiscal year 2025/26 compared with the previous fiscal year, according to figures presented at the company’s 23rd annual general meeting. Company Chairman said Indian nationals accounted for 29 percent of total passengers, with visitors arriving from Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Jharkhand, Bihar, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh. Many visitors travel to Basantapur Hill in Palpa to visit the Kamaksha Temple and the historic Durga Temple. To attract more Indian tourists, the company has strengthened coordination with drivers operating across the border and expanded digital promotional campaigns involving regional vloggers. Meanwhile, plans for a five-star hotel and casino complex at the cable car’s upper station have advanced to the design approval stage. Additional attractions, including roller coasters and zero-gravity rides, are also planned. The company has established promotional partnerships with more than 70 hotels, 40 institutions and 45 educational organisations in Butwal and Bhairahawa to further expand its reach.

Banke farmers expand Kalanamak rice cultivation as prices reach Rs 12,000 per quintal

Farmers in Banke district are expanding the cultivation of Kalanamak rice, a fragrant and flavourful traditional variety that commands a premium price in the market. One farmer, who initially cultivated the variety on 677.26 square metres of land, has expanded the area to 3,386.29 square metres to take advantage of growing demand. While hybrid rice varieties generally sell for Rs 3,000 to Rs 3,200 per quintal, Kalanamak fetches around Rs 12,000 per quintal. The crop produces soft, aromatic grains and takes approximately 140 days to mature after transplantation. Farmers generally plant it in Ashad and harvest it in late Kartik. A farmer reportedly expects to harvest 15 quintals from 20 kilograms of seed, although the production estimate should be verified. Commercial cultivation is also underway across 20,317.88 square metres in Gurwa village of Janaki Rural Municipality-5. The chief of the Agriculture Knowledge Centre in Nepalgunj said programmes promoting indigenous crop varieties were helping farmers expand production. Cultivation is particularly concentrated in Kohalpur Municipality and Baijanath Rural Municipality.

‘Kabaddi 5’ crosses Rs 70 million at domestic box office

The Nepali film Kabaddi 5, written and directed by Ram Babu Gurung, has grossed more than Rs 70 million at the domestic box office, according to its producer. Producer Maniram Pokharel said the film had earned more than Rs 50 million by Sunday and continued to perform strongly through Tuesday. The movie has received encouraging responses from audiences and critics, with more than 60 screenings reportedly sold out by Tuesday morning. Its box-office earnings are expected to rise further, as cinemas across the country are offering discounted tickets on Wednesday and Thursday. The film features Dayahang Rai, Bijay Baral, Buddhi Tamang, Srijana Gurung and Bipin Karki, among others. It is presented by Bansuri Films and produced by Ram Babu Gurung, Maniram Pokharel, Madhu Mijar and Bishal Gurung.

Him Parbat Hydropower opens IPO for project-affected residents and migrant workers

Him Parbat Hydropower Company has opened its initial public offering (IPO) for residents of project-affected areas and Nepali citizens working abroad. The company, which has an issued capital of Rs 1.69 billion, is offering 5,915,000 ordinary shares worth Rs 591.5 million at a face value of Rs 100 per share as part of its planned public issuance. Of the total offering, 1,690,000 shares worth Rs 169 million have been allocated to residents of project-affected areas. This includes 1,014,000 shares for permanent residents of severely affected areas in Bigu Rural Municipality wards 5, 6, 7 and 8, and Kalinchowk Rural Municipality wards 2, 3 and 4 in Dolakha district. Another 676,000 shares have been reserved for residents of other designated wards. An additional 422,500 shares, worth Rs 42.25 million, have been set aside for Nepali citizens employed abroad who hold valid foreign employment permits. Applications from local residents will remain open until November 11, while eligible migrant workers must apply by November 2. Citizens Capital is managing the issue, with applications accepted through designated banking partners, including Citizens Bank, Prabhu Bank, Sindhu Development Bank and Laxmi Sunrise Bank.

title: Nepal's India reset should be national, not partisan - Nepali Times
description: Nepal's India reset should be national, not partisan  Nepali Times
publisher.title: Nepali Times
full_article:
Eight months ago in this space, I argued that Nepal's crisis is better explained by homegrown institutional decay than by ‘foreign hands’. And here we go again: the India question is back at the centre of our politics.

Not through a foreign plot this time, but through a minister's words in Delhi. At the NDTV World Summit last week, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, who is also vice-chair of the RSP, said: "Our generation is different. We have seen the world, and our aspirations are economic. We want good jobs, good governance and good relations with our neighbours. So I can say with great happiness that the era of associating Nepali nationalism with anti-Indianism is now over."

Picture the scene. A globetrotting, highly capable Nepali economist and finance minister takes the limelight with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. He hit all the right chords, with a confidence rarely seen in Nepali dignitaries. So what could go wrong?

Well, for all the good intentions, a single word threw a spoke in an otherwise smoothly turning wheel. That word was "anti-Indianism" Back home, the reaction was swift. Critics asked why such a claim had to be made on a foreign platform.

Nepal needs a constructive and confident relationship with India, built on trade, energy, tourism, connectivity, IT parks and mutual respect. In an op-ed in Nepali Times back in 2010 titled ‘Win-win-win’, I proposed a trilateral connectivity and economic-cooperation summit among China, Nepal and India.

Nepal political culture labels people ‘pro-China’ and ‘pro-India’ against each other while opportunities next door is wasted. In that light, Wagle was trying to project a reset that his party had already articulated: Nepal as a ‘vibrant bridge’.

With a little less bravado, he could have achieved the same goal without the slippage. How can a government announce a change in foreign policy without turning it into another partisan wedge issue back home.

Read generously, his message was a generational one. Wagle’s implication seemed to be that his party's sweeping electoral support was proof that voters had rejected that old party-machine culture altogether.

Last September’s uprising and the sweeping mandate given to the RSP were largely a rejection of the moral decay, governance failures and extractive politics of the past, not a referendum on Nepal's relations with India or China.

Still, a new party with such a mandate naturally wants a fresh start with our southern neighbour, drawing on shared history and geography for mutual benefit, and to stand apart from the old pro-India and anti-India camps altogether. That is a worthy ambition.

But there is a boundary democracies have long tried to respect, and much of the criticism of Wagle's Delhi flap can be understood in that light.

In 2020, after the map dispute with India, the Nepali Congress' Minendra Rijal defended Nepal's position on Indian television. Though one of Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli's fiercest critics at home, he made clear that his opposition stopped at Nepal's borders.

Wagle did not attack his rivals by name, and his purpose was clearly to reinforce the idea of development diplomacy. But a minister abroad speaks for the country, not just his party, as others have noted. In going the extra mile to make his point, he used a word that may have blurred the line between a national message and a partisan one, perhaps unintentionally.

Here is the irony: to declare Nepal free of the old labels, many saw him as reaching for one of them. ‘Anti-Indianism’ is not a neutral description of the past. In our politics it is an accusation, and it is often aimed at someone.

Had Wagle simply said that Nepal is moving from the ‘politics of grievance’ to ‘development diplomacy’, his message would have come through clearly. ‘Anti-Indianism’ turned it into a quarrel over domestic dispute played out on foreign soil.

For decades, the far left and the far right branded the NC as ‘pro-India’, and it turn the party cast its rivals as ‘anti-India’. Each label serves the same purpose: to paint the other side as less patriotic.

When that vocabulary travels to a neighbour's capital, it sends a mixed signal about whom the neighbour should be dealing with: the party or the state. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal's recent engagement with Delhi went through the proper channels, and one hopes that is the message India takes away: Nepal's partner is the state, not a party or its personalities.

None of this means anti-India sentiment was simply invented. The 2015 bBlockade was real, and its hardship is remembered in every Nepali kitchen. Unresolved issues remain: the border, unilateral embankments that flood the Tarai, barriers to our electricity, stalemate on air corridors. Raising them is not hostility. It is the duty of any government.

Former Indian ambassador Ranjit Rae, in his memoir Kathmandu Dilemma, gives his account of Nepali politicians seeking India House's views even on appointments such as the police chief. The north is no different. During the Communist split of 2020–21, China's ambassador was lobbying openly to hold the party together. Political factions have often courted one neighbour while accusing rivals of serving the other. It is our political culture.

When our institutions are weak, foreign governments find it easier to deal with individual leaders and party networks than with the state itself. Our politicians, in turn, have been accused of seeking outside relationships to strengthen their hand at home.

Critics back home saw a Nepal minister trying to win favour abroad by casting others as an anti-India faction. Whether intended or not, such political messaging risks turning relations with a neighbour into a tool of domestic party competition. Over time, this can weaken Nepal's bargaining position and give outside powers greater leverage over our internal politics.

The RSP's manifesto promises to turn Nepal from a buffer state into a ‘vibrant bridge’ between India and China. Wagle's message was trying to achieve just that: collaboration, growth and opportunity. I welcome that. But a bridge must be trusted by both banks of a river, and any shift in relations with India should be seen as Nepal's national policy, not just the RSP's party position.

To be fair to Wagle, every new government wants to show how it differs from the past. And sometimes that means pointing out what went wrong before. But foreign policy must go beyond party politics. Governments may change, but Nepal's national interests remain. The challenge is to improve relations with India without making it seem like one party speaks for Nepal more than others.

Democracies need not speak with one voice. Debate and opposition are healthy, especially at home. But looking outward, Nepal needs a foreign policy that continues from one government to the next.

Perhaps the most hopeful part of Wagle's message was not about India at all. It was about Nepal's younger generation: the demands for jobs, opportunity and accountable government. Whether this also marks a retreat from the old pro-India and anti-India labels remains to be seen. But it offers an opportunity to focus on economic ties with both neighbours that benefit ordinary Nepalis.

That is a message worth carrying abroad to both capitals. A statement this bold was made in Delhi, a similar one belongs in Beijing: Nepal's patriotism should not be measured by how close or distant it is from either neighbor, it should be a national message.

Our neighbours, too, should deal with Nepal through its institutions rather than through favoured parties or leaders. And our politicians should stop turning legitimate national concerns into tests of partisan patriotism.

Can Nepal change its foreign-policy direction without making every change of government a new declaration of who is patriotic and who is not? The younger generation may be opening that door. Whether our political institutions can follow remains the harder question.

For better or worse, the end of anti-India nationalism will not be declared in Delhi. It will be earned at home: in power plants, factories, export markets, and institutions strong enough to outlast any party.

title: Kolkata E-Cigarette Seizure Uncovers ₹13.5 Crore Haul in Nepal-Bound Containers - Maritime Gateway
description: Kolkata E-Cigarette Seizure Uncovers ₹13.5 Crore Haul in Nepal-Bound Containers  Maritime Gateway
publisher.title: Maritime Gateway
full_article:
Summary

The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence seized approximately 55,000 e-cigarettes valued at ₹13.5 crore from two Nepal-bound transshipment containers at Kolkata’s Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port. Officers found the devices concealed among cargo declared as drinking glasses and ceramic mugs during examinations conducted on 24 October 2026.

Intelligence-led checks uncover concealed shipments

The Kolkata e-cigarette seizure followed specific intelligence that two containers moving through the port as Nepal-bound transshipment consignments contained prohibited products.

DRI officers intercepted the containers and conducted detailed examinations. One consignment had been declared as “water glass”, while the other was declared as “ceramic mugs”.

The first container yielded 40,000 IGET-brand e-cigarettes in various flavours. Officers recovered approximately 15,000 additional devices from the second container, including products bearing the VTV, VOKO, Bang and Ejoy brands.

The e-cigarettes were concealed among the declared goods, which served as cover cargo. DRI seized both the devices and the accompanying cargo under relevant provisions of the Customs Act.

The agency disclosed the operations in an announcement issued on 28 October.

Consignments were declared for onward movement to Nepal

The containers’ declared destination was Nepal, making the interceptions relevant to the monitoring of goods moving through India under transshipment arrangements.

The announcement does not identify the consignors, consignees, shipping lines, customs brokers or countries of origin. It also does not state whether the two consignments were connected.

No arrests, prosecution details or findings establishing individual responsibility were disclosed.

The Nepal-bound declaration should therefore be treated as the consignments’ stated routing. The announcement does not establish that the devices were intended for diversion into India, nor does it identify their eventual customers.

What DRI has reported is the discovery of concealed e-cigarettes behind declarations describing different goods. Further findings would be required to establish the full commercial and logistical chain.

Seizures form part of wider enforcement activity

DRI said it had seized approximately 300,000 e-cigarettes valued at more than ₹120 crore during FY2026–27 across ports, airports and inland container depots.

The locations covered Maharashtra, Gujarat, Delhi and West Bengal, indicating enforcement activity across several cargo gateways and transport channels.

These are reported seizure totals, rather than an estimate of the overall illicit market. They do not establish how many prohibited devices may have escaped detection.

The announcement also does not clarify whether the latest Kolkata haul is included in the financial-year figures. The quantities should consequently not be added together without further confirmation.

Similarly, the ₹13.5 crore valuation describes DRI’s assessment of the seized e-cigarettes. It should not be presented as customs revenue recovered or a penalty imposed.

India’s prohibition dates to 2019

India prohibits the production, manufacture, import, export, transport, sale, distribution, storage and advertisement of electronic cigarettes under legislation enacted in 2019.

The prohibition covers electronic nicotine delivery systems and related devices. Government guidance identifies the legislation as a public-health measure and states that contraventions are punishable under its provisions.

The policy originated in an ordinance promulgated in September 2019, followed by the legislation. The government’s stated concerns included nicotine addiction, uptake among young people and the implications for tobacco-control efforts.

In the Kolkata operations, DRI specifically reported seizure under the Customs Act. The announcement does not set out individual charges under the electronic-cigarette legislation or disclose the outcome of any adjudication.

Misdeclaration places cargo accuracy in focus

For the maritime logistics industry, the case highlights the importance of accurate commodity descriptions and consistency between shipping documents and physical cargo.

Declarations identifying ordinary household goods can conceal a materially different consignment. In these operations, intelligence-led examination allowed officers to establish what was actually inside the containers.

The seizure does not, by itself, establish wrongdoing by every business involved in handling or transporting them. Responsibility will depend on evidence concerning the preparation, declaration and movement of each consignment.

The next substantive developments would be identification of the parties responsible, clarification of links between the containers and any resulting enforcement proceedings. Until those details emerge, the confirmed outcome remains the seizure of approximately 55,000 concealed devices and their cover cargo.

FAQs

Where and when did the seizures take place?

At Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata, on 24 October 2026.

How many e-cigarettes were recovered?

Approximately 55,000: 40,000 from one container and around 15,000 from another.

What goods had been declared?

The declarations described “water glass” and “ceramic mugs”.

Were the containers destined for Nepal?

They were declared as Nepal-bound transshipment consignments.

Were any arrests announced?

The supplied announcement did not disclose arrests or identify the parties responsible.

title: Rain expected across Nepal on Thursday as cyclone weakens - The Kathmandu Post
description: Rain expected across Nepal on Thursday as cyclone weakens  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Although Cyclone Arnab has weakened into a low-pressure system, its remnants are expected to bring rain to several parts of Nepal from Thursday afternoon, with the risk of heavy rainfall increasing overnight and into Friday.

Meteorologist Binod Pokharel said people should remain alert from Thursday night through Saturday morning, as the system could bring heavy rain to multiple locations. Cloud cover has begun to increase under its influence, but no rain had been reported in Nepal as of Thursday morning.

The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology has also forecast that the system’s influence will gradually intensify from Thursday.

According to the department, most places in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces could receive moderate rain accompanied by thunder and lightning, as well as snowfall, from October 29 to 31.

Many places in Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces could also experience moderate rain, hailstorms, thunder and lightning, along with snowfall.

The department has warned of heavy rain and snowfall at a few places in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces. One or two places in the mountainous and hilly areas of Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces could also receive heavy rain and snowfall.

Pokharel said Thursday’s forecast identified fewer at-risk districts than Wednesday’s, but the low-pressure system covered a large area. Its interaction with an upper-atmospheric trough could trigger heavy rainfall in several locations, he said.
